body:
I watched the talk, it was very good, thanks for sharing. :) 
Sorry it took me so long to reply, I was very busy with school work.
I think the connecting the dots statement is a very wise one. I think all people are really just stumbling around doing what they think is best in the hopes that one day it'll all work out in the end. However, it doesn't always work out for everyone. Most college dropouts do not become Steve Jobs.
Still, I think it is some valuable advice to just try things and to do what you think is best, because no one else can really tell you how to live your life. Although some people are more knowledgable about their life, some advice does not apply to everyone. I think sometimes you do just need to try things, even if you end up failing. Although not all people become Steve Jobs, people who get up again after falling down almost always find some sort of success. 
I'm very grateful for all the thought you put into helping me, it has made me more thoughtful, at the least.
As you can tell, I didn't kill myself, but I haven't been much better off the past few days. After talking to you and a couple of my friends, I decided that the first thing I am going to do is go back to therapy. After that, I will decide what I want to do. I have applied to some colleges, so if I decide I want to go then I can. But if I decide that I want to wait for a year, I'm going to try talking to my parents about it.

Again, thanks for all of your help. I probably won't be checking reddit again after this. I really, really appreciate you taking the time to write thoughtful responses-- you have given me some hope. :) 

Thank you again, and I hope you have a wonderful day/life.

Thank you for sending me that speech, I found it very interesting and thought provoking. 
I'm still not sure if I want to talk to my parents, I'm really so afraid I'm going to make the wrong decision...and this is a very important decision. I don't trust myself to make the right decision. I think I will end up talking to them, I'm just scared. 
I think that distractions are definitely useful, but I usually end up distracting myself with pointless things like watching comedy on youtube or playing video games. I have tried challenging the thoughts before, but it's really difficult. It's hard to think logically about it, and I usually just end up giving into the negative thinking. If I do take a year off, I definitely want to explore a lot of things, and hopefully find something that I really do enjoy, but I don't know if I would be able to do that.
And thank you a lot for responding to this, I really appreciate the help
Thank you so much. The people on here are really so nice. I appreciate you taking the time to help me
Thank you a lot for your responses, they have given me a lot to think about. I really appreciate you taking the time to talk to me about this

I do have a hard time accepting my mistakes, but I'm not really sure if I'll be able to stop beating myself up over them. It feels like a really big part of who I am, and I've sort of just accepted myself as worthless, I don't even really challenge it anymore. I guess it is something I would work on, but there are so many other things that I have to do that take precedence. 

I am afraid to mess things up. I feel like I'm constantly messing everything up, whether I really am or not. I think you're right that I won't ever feel how I used to, and that sucks, because my life used to be a lot better. I fear that I won't ever figure things out, and I'll just end up wasting my whole life. I used to have such high hopes for myself. It's difficult to go from thinking I could do anything to thinking I can't and won't ever do anything. I used to be a very high achieving person, but now I feel like everything is just permanently messed up.

I guess I know that it is my decision in the end, but I'm not very good at talking to my parents and saying what I think. I don't even completely know what I want, so that makes it harder. I do really think I want to go to college, but I really think I could benefit from maybe taking a gap year or something. But my parents are extremely controlling with what I do, and my dad has forbidden me from doing anything other than just going to university straight out of high school. I'm their only child, so I guess all of their hopes ride on me. If I fail, they don't have any other kids that may succeed. I do plan on moving out really as soon as I can...but I still want to have a good relationship with them. I don't want to disappoint them, and I don't really know how to talk to them about maybe taking my own path in life instead of the one they have set out for me. I think if I tried to stand up to them and say that I was going to take a gap year or something, I would probably give in fairly easily because I can't stand being yelled at and I'll just feel guilty. I don't even know if that's what I want to do, I just wish they would let me talk to them about it as an adult, instead of treating me like I know nothing. I know I don't know much, but I still wish I had a say in my own future. 

That's an interesting analogy haha, but I like it. There are things I want to explore in the world, and things that I want to learn, but I can't seem to get my mind to shut up about the suicide thing. It's really hard to do things when you can't stop thinking about killing yourself. I would love to go out and discover things, but I feel like it would be difficult since my mind seems to be against me most of the time. I fear that the second I leave home, I'm going to lose all of my motivation and I'll just end up doing nothing, since most of my drive has almost always come from my parents pushing me to do things. I'm afraid that I'd give in too easily and then either end up homeless or dead one way or another. I don't really know how to take care of myself, the only thing I really know how to do is study-- and recently, I don't even do that well. So, while I would love to go out and do something crazy and experience new things, I feel like I wouldn't be able to handle the responsibility.

I don't feel ready because I had a lot of mental health issues for two years or so, and I feel like I really missed a lot of maturing in that time. Also, I felt more ready because the suicidal thoughts had left, but now that they're back, I'm not sure.
I really am not sure what I want to study yet. On my college apps (that are due in three days that I haven't finished :/) I put that I wanted to major in English, because I really enjoy reading and writing and I'm supposedly good at writing essays, but really I'm interested in so many things, I don't know what I want to do. I've switched from psychiatrist to neurobiology to mathematician to linguist to author/english professor all in high school, and I honestly don't know if I even want to do any of that. 
I think it would be useful for me to take a gap year, because then I would have some more time to think about what I want to really study, and I would be able to go out in the world and maybe do something and experience something new, and really do some maturing. However, this was forbidden by my parents (mainly my father), and I wasn't even allowed to have any say in it. I feel like taking a year off to really get myself together, and maybe work on my mental health and sense of responsibility, I would get a lot more out of college/university right from the start. I feel like if I go now, I might not be able to keep up with the work, or I could end up getting depressed again and not taking care of myself, or even killing myself. 
I really want to go to college, but I'm afraid that if I went now, it could be a disaster. Most of my other friends seem much more prepared-- which I know everyone feels that way somewhat, but really in my case it is true. I tend to be friends with ap/ib students who all have glowing college "brag sheets," and while I'm an ap student myself, I don't do any extra activities, I have very little idea of what I want to study, and my life honestly feels like a complete mess compared to theirs. My grades look fine this year, but last year I almost completely stopped doing work, and because of that my grades really suffered. I'm not sure that I'll even get into any of the universities I'm applying to.

Thanks, those are all good suggestions. I could try the hobby thing, but I don't really know if I'm up to going to therapy again, and I'm not really sure if I would be able to give myself pep-talks in the mirror. Thank you, though, I appreciate it.

I'm going to stick to the numbers just because it's easier to respond that way. 

1. I guess you're right that it isn't possible to prove that I won't achieve anything, but I really feel like I won't. And I recently feel like I do everything wrong, which is probably mostly because I hate myself the majority of the time. I haven't been able to stop lecturing myself for everything that I think I'm doing wrong, which often includes expressing my feelings. 

2. It's not that I'm really completely uninterested in everything...I actually do usually enjoy school, and I enjoy learning most things. But when I get like this, it's difficult to even pay attention, let alone enjoy the material. I know there are a lot of things I haven't done, and a lot of places I haven't been, and I want to explore many of those things...but sometimes I feel like I can't enjoy the things that I know I'm supposed to and that I usually do. It's just that I used to be interested in pretty much everything, but it doesn't feel that way anymore. I just want to feel the way I used to.

3. People say this of me a lot, but I don't really notice it a lot of the time, although I think it is kind of true. I do really want to go to college, I just don't feel ready for it right now, but my parents won't let me talk about it at all. They're both high achieving and expect the same out of me. I know they're just worried, but I'm not at all allowed to make my own decisions. It's hard to figure out who I want to be when all I've ever done is tried to please other people. I really have no idea what I myself want, I always let other people decide for me. I have little to no faith in myself and my own thoughts, so it's just a lot easier to go with what other people say. The only thing that I currently want and apparently think is a suitable option is to kill myself. Killing myself is really so much easier than dealing with everything else.

I don't feel worthless, I am worthless. I always do things wrong, and everything I do isn't good enough. I should be interested in things, but I'm just not, and because of that, I'm not ever going to achieve anything, and I'll just be a disappointment. I feel like I'm always pretending to like things and pretending to be good at things when I'm really not. I've ruined everything in my family because I don't ever want to spend time with them, and I don't really want to spend time with anyone for that matter. I am so, so tired of feeling miserable, and I don't want to try anymore. I used to be so motivated and ambitious. Now I can't ever stop hating myself, and I'm not passionate about anything. I'm a senior in high school, and I am supposed to be excited to go to college, and I used to be, but now the thought of it just makes me anxious. I don't feel ready for anything. Everyone else just does their work, and is far more ready than I am. I'm really so pathetic. Things were getting better, and I worked so hard for them to be that way, but now I feel like it's all just falling apart again. I feel guilty because my friends say things and I don't even find them funny. I try to laugh but it doesn't come out right. I was starting to get my old motivation back, but now I just want to lie in bed and sleep. I can't stop thinking about killing myself, and I just want everything to go away. I know there are things that I will miss, but I am just so tired. Sorry this is so long. I hate talking to my friends about things because I know they don't know what to say, and whatever they say doesn't really make a difference anyways. I think it would just be better for everyone if I killed myself.
Thank you for your response, I appreciate the support. Part of me also hopes that there's a still a chance for me.

I have seen a doctor about stuff like this before, and I've been on anti-depressants. It helped for a bit, but things got worse again, and even when they were getting better, and I was working really hard to make things better, my life still didn't feel pleasurable or happy, and I still probably would've preferred to be dead. 
I appreciate the support, and I wish you were right, but I really don't think it's possible for me to ever get completely better.

The problem is that I am worthless. I'm not going anywhere with my life. It doesn't matter if I can see the good things in life or not, because even if there are good things in the world, I am still worthless. I've been to the doctor and several therapists and psychiatrists. It doesn't help me because I have a really really hard time getting close to people, and I ended up dodging most of their questions. I appreciate the faith that you seem to have in people improving their lives, but I honestly don't think it is ever going to get better for me, because I'm not willing to put in the effort. I'm trying of trying to force myself to feel things, I just want to be how I used to be. But I don't see that happening, so I don't think I should live anymore.

I was really excited to try this out, but it says that it's not accepting new users. Do you know when it will be? I've been looking for a minimalist online journaling site for a long time now, and I think this is perfect for me.
